name: SQLite
tagline: The in-process SQL engine that ships in every phone, browser and OS: one file, zero servers.
description: SQLite is a self-contained C library that implements a full transactional SQL database in a single cross-platform file. It is the most widely deployed database in the world, embedded in Android, iOS, every major browser, desktop apps and countless devices, and it has become a serious option for server-side apps too, thanks to WAL mode, litestream-style replication and the libSQL/Turso ecosystem. The code is in the public domain and maintained by a small team at Hwaci that does not accept outside patches, with an exhaustive test suite backing its reliability. It is ideal when the database lives next to the application; it is not a networked multi-writer server.

pricing.notes: Public domain. Optional paid support, encryption extension (SEE) and Consortium membership from Hwaci.

scale.notes: Databases up to terabytes are possible, but one writer at a time; replication needs external tools (Litestream, LiteFS, rqlite).

strengths: Zero configuration: the whole database is one portable file
Extremely well tested (100% branch coverage, billions of deployments)
In-process calls avoid network round trips, so simple reads take microseconds
FTS5, JSON functions and R*Tree indexes built into the amalgamation
Public domain with a stable file format guaranteed through 2050
weaknesses: Single writer at a time; write-heavy concurrent workloads serialize
No built-in network server, user accounts or replication
Dynamic typing by default surprises people used to strict schemas (STRICT tables help)
ALTER TABLE support is limited compared with server databases
useCases: Test fixtures and data interchange files
Low-to-moderate traffic web apps on a single server
notIdealFor: Many concurrent writers across processes or hosts
Multi-tenant client-server deployments needing access control
